notes: Access: plain direct HTTP fetch, no WAF/bot-block, robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (confirmed same as prior Home-Decor pass). Discovered via the category sitemap (sitemap_0.xml, matched on 'best-sellers'/'best-sell'). Found a genuine 2-tier taxonomy: parent 'Best Sellers' (https://www.surlatable.com/products/best-sellers/, canonical, react-helmet title 'Best Sellers') which itself links to 8 department-scoped children at /best-sellers/<dept>/. Verified each department child is a genuine site-defined taxonomy node, not a filter/sort artifact: page's own embedded pageData JSON shows breadCrumbs=['Home','Products','Best Sellers','<Dept>'], categoryID='best-seller-<dept>', pageType='product listing' for every child (e.g. Coffee & Tea child categoryID='best-seller-coffee'). Each child page is rendered on an older SFRA-style template (results-hits pagination block '1-24 of N Results') while the parent uses the newer PWA-kit template ('N Items' header + 'Showing 24 of N' footer) - different templates but both are real, distinct, browsable PLPs. Sum of the 8 children (490) does not equal the parent's own count (464); this is expected since the parent is a separate overall best-seller index (different underlying product population/rotation) from the per-department best-seller views, not an aggregation of them - not treated as an error. Checked and EXCLUDED as not genuine Bestsellers PLPs: /slt-favorites/ (title 'Sur La Table Favorites' but 0 product links and no h1/product grid in the rendered HTML - an editorial/marketing page, not a listing), /registry-favorites*/ (gift-registry curation pages, not merchandising bestsellers), 'Sales & Special Offers' /sale/ and its many sub-pages (promotional Sale, covered under Clearance brief's own Sale-vs-Clearance test, not Bestsellers). Site search was not used since robots.txt disallows /search*; navigation/sitemap/breadcrumb evidence was sufficient and is the stronger signal per project rules anyway. No local-language variants applicable (US English-only site).
